title: The Epilogue
question: Today, can the narrator trust that the living world around him is real?
light: green lamplight and hazy sun, deep black shadows
palette: lamp green, mahogany, olive green, slate-blue haze, brass, deep black

study_essay.described: An upstairs study at night at the back of a red-brick Maybury villa. A mahogany writing-table with a green leather top stands a yard before a pair of glazed French windows, each leaf of six panes, with a low wrought-iron rail, cream curtains drawn back on a brass pole and a raised holland blind. On the table stand a brass oil lamp with a green glass shade, stacked manuscript sheets, a brass inkstand and a translucent selenite paperweight, with a leather-seated swivel chair on the room side. An oak bookcase and a terrestrial globe stand against the right wall, a red-and-blue Turkey carpet covers the floor, and olive-green and gold paper covers the walls. Green-gold lamplight falls from the lamp at the table's left end across the papers and throws the long shadow of the chair back toward the camera; the window glass holds a dark green valley with scattered lit windows under the stars.
study_essay.landmark: the brass oil lamp with the green glass shade
study_essay.route: from the landing door across the Turkey carpet to the writing-table under the French windows
study_essay.geometry: The French windows fill the CENTRE of the far wall, filling the TOP half of the frame from the left third to the right third. The writing-table crosses the lower CENTRE at half the frame's width, its lamp at the LEFT end of the tabletop a tenth of the frame's height. The chair stands at the BOTTOM edge in the centre, its back a fifth of the frame's height. The bookcase and globe stand along the RIGHT edge at a third of the frame's height. The Turkey carpet fills the BOTTOM edge between the chair and the camera.
study_essay.ambience: a clock ticking on the mantel, a steel pen scratching on paper, the faint hiss of the oil lamp, night wind at the window glass

study_table.described: The mahogany writing-table of a Victorian study at night, seen along its length from the fireplace side. Its green leather top holds stacked manuscript sheets in black ink, a brass double inkwell with two steel pens, a translucent white selenite paperweight, a few cloth-bound books and a brass oil lamp with a green glass shade. A leather-seated desk chair stands pulled back from the near side. Behind the table rise the edge of a glazed French window with a cream curtain and a starry night sky in the panes, and in the corner beyond stand an oak bookcase and a terrestrial globe on a stand. The lamp at the near LEFT throws green-gold light along the tabletop toward the window and casts long shadows of the inkwell and the books to the RIGHT, leaving the far corner in deep black.
study_table.landmark: the brass oil lamp with the green glass shade
study_table.route: along the tabletop from the lamp past the manuscript stack to the window corner
study_table.geometry: The tabletop runs from the BOTTOM LEFT corner toward the TOP RIGHT, filling the lower half of the frame. The brass lamp stands at the LEFT edge, its green shade a quarter of the frame's height. The manuscript stack sits in the CENTRE at a fifth of the frame's width, the inkwell and the selenite paperweight just to its right. The window edge and cream curtain rise along the RIGHT third to the TOP edge; the globe and bookcase stand small in the TOP LEFT corner beyond the lamp.
study_table.ambience: a clock ticking on the mantel, a steel pen scratching on paper, the faint hiss of the oil lamp, a page turning

study_window.described: The view from the open French windows of an upstairs study over a Surrey valley at night. The painted window frame and a low wrought-iron rail stand in the foreground. Below lie a dark lawn and the rounded tops of tall beech trees; beyond them a railway cutting with a brick arch and a signal gantry carrying red, green and yellow lamps. At the left the lit houses about Woking station cluster beside a domed mosque and a college tower; in the centre distance a broad dark heath shows pale sand-pits; at the right stand black pine woods. A clear sky full of stars spans the top, a small red point of Mars low in it. Cold starlight falls from the upper RIGHT across the sill, throwing the shadows of the window bars inward onto the floorboards, and the lit windows below glow orange against the black of the woods.
study_window.landmark: the brick railway arch below the hill
study_window.route: from the window rail down across the lawn and the beech tops to the railway arch and the heath beyond
study_window.geometry: The window frame borders all four edges, its wrought-iron rail crossing the BOTTOM quarter. Beech tops fill the lower third as a dark band. The brick railway arch stands in the CENTRE just below the middle at a tenth of the frame's width, the signal lamps to its right. The pale sand-pits lie in the centre distance; black pine woods fill the RIGHT third. Stars fill the TOP half.
study_window.ambience: night wind in the beeches, a distant goods train on the line, an owl in the pines, curtains stirring at the frame

primrose_summit.described: The summit of Primrose Hill on a hazy day, a public park again. Level lawns and oval flower beds of red geraniums and white alyssum, edged with clipped box, line a gravel path set with iron benches. On the crest stands the fighting-machine, a weathered brass hood on three long jointed legs, enclosed by a low iron railing with a small painted notice board at its gate. Beyond the crest the great province of London houses lies dim and blue through a soft haze of smoke and mist, roofs and chimneys fading into the lower sky. Hazy sun falls from the upper LEFT and throws the long shadows of the machine's three legs across the lawns to the RIGHT, and the shade under the hood is a deep black against the pale sky. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT, deep shadow.
primrose_summit.landmark: the fighting-machine behind its low iron railing
primrose_summit.route: along the gravel path from the flower beds up to the iron railing round the fighting-machine
primrose_summit.geometry: The gravel path enters at the BOTTOM centre and runs up to the RIGHT third. Oval flower beds of red geraniums fill the BOTTOM LEFT and BOTTOM RIGHT corners. The fighting-machine stands in the RIGHT third behind its railing, its hood reaching the TOP edge and its legs half the frame's height. Iron benches line the path's left side at a tenth of the frame's height. London's blue haze of roofs fills a band across the CENTRE from the LEFT edge to the machine's legs, the pale sky across the TOP third.
primrose_summit.crowd: about thirty sight-seers in summer dress stand in loose knots about the iron railing and stroll the gravel path, and six children run and chase between the flower beds, all small in the distance
primrose_summit.ambience: children shouting at play, footsteps on gravel, larks over the grass, wind in the grass, a far hum of the city

study_reverse.described: A Victorian study at night seen from beside its French windows, looking back into the room. In the foreground stand the back of a leather-seated desk chair and the edge of a mahogany writing-table under a green-shaded brass lamp. Across the room floor-to-ceiling oak bookcases hold cloth-bound volumes, with a framed engraving of Charles Darwin on the end panel and a small leather armchair before it. At the left a panelled door stands ajar onto a dark landing; at the right a small black cast-iron fireplace with a slate mantel holds a clock and a pipe rack, a star chart framed above it. The green-shaded lamp at the near LEFT throws warm light across the tabletop and casts the chair's long shadow over the Turkey carpet toward the bookcases, while the grate glows a low red at the RIGHT and the landing beyond the door is deep black.
study_reverse.landmark: the black cast-iron fireplace with the clock on its slate mantel
study_reverse.route: from the panelled landing door across the Turkey carpet to the desk chair by the window
study_reverse.geometry: The desk chair's back and the table's edge with the lamp fill the BOTTOM LEFT corner at a third of the frame's height. The oak bookcases fill the CENTRE of the far wall from the left third to the right third, the Darwin engraving and the leather armchair before it at a fifth of the frame's height. The panelled door stands ajar at the LEFT edge onto the dark landing. The fireplace with its clock and star chart stands at the RIGHT edge at a quarter of the frame's height.
study_reverse.ambience: a clock ticking on the mantel, coals settling in the grate, night wind at the window, a chair creaking

it is to stand on Primrose Hill, as I did but a day before writing this last chapter
shots.turn: a haunted city -> a sunny park; the crowds look like ghosts to him
shots.why: London is busy again, but to him the crowds walk a dead city; the machine still stands among the flowers.

shots.frame: Medium on the low iron railing round the fighting-machine, its small painted notice board at the gate, red geraniums and white alyssum along its base, two jointed brass legs rising behind.
shots.motion: The camera rises above the geraniums across the whole shot, looking down over the iron railing and the painted notice board; the wind bends the geranium heads along the railing; the wind runs on through the white alyssum at the railing's base
shots.camera: On the gravel path outside the railing, standing chest height, three yards from the gate, a 40mm lens; hazy sun comes from the upper LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the red geraniums along the BOTTOM edge at the base of the low iron railing, white alyssum between them. The small painted notice board hangs on the railing gate at the CENTRE, and two of the machine's jointed brass legs rise at the RIGHT third to the TOP edge behind it.
shots.end: The iron railing and its painted notice board cross the CENTRE seen from above, the geraniums along the BOTTOM edge, the long shadows of the brass legs across the gravel at the RIGHT third.

sounds.sound: children shouting and laughing at play

source: I go to London and see the busy multitudes in Fleet Street and the Strand
it is to stand on Primrose Hill, as I did but a day before writing this last chapter
shots.turn: a haunted city -> a sunny park; the crowds look like ghosts to him
shots.why: The voices of the crowd play over a railed-off relic: to him the living walk a dead city, and the machine is a garden ornament.

shots.frame: Medium of the narrator (grey eyes, ash-grey moustache, boater with a black band) walking up the gravel path, and a pace behind him the wife (wide hazel eyes, thick chestnut-auburn hair, sage-green wool skirt) with her shawl in rust and cream over her arm.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the narrator as he walks up the gravel path toward the iron railing across the whole shot; the narrator turns from the fighting-machine to the wife and reaches back for her hand; the wife steps up to him, her shawl swinging at her arm
shots.camera: Beside the gravel path at the narrator's right, standing head height, three yards from him, a 40mm lens; hazy sun comes from the upper LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator at the LEFT third, his head a fifth of the frame's height, his face turned up toward the fighting-machine's legs at the TOP RIGHT. The wife walks a pace behind him at the RIGHT third, smaller in the frame, and red geraniums line the BOTTOM edge.
shots.end: The narrator stands at the CENTRE facing the wife at the RIGHT third, his hand holding hers between them, the machine's brass legs at the TOP edge behind.
source: to see the people walking to and fro among the flower beds on the hill
shots.turn: the machine's pull -> the living woman; he chooses her over the wreck
shots.why: The turn: among the ghosts and the old machine, he reaches for the one person he had counted dead.

shots.frame: Insert on the fighting-machine's jointed brass foot sunk in the turf behind the low iron railing, red geraniums at the railing's base.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right, past the machine, travelling a forearm, across the whole shot; the wind bends the geraniums at the railing; hazy sunlight glints along the dented brass plates
shots.camera: Outside the iron railing, kneeling height, two yards from the foot, a 50mm lens looking up; hazy sun comes from the upper LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the weathered brass foot of the fighting-machine at the CENTRE, sunk in the turf, its jointed leg rising out of the TOP edge. The low iron railing crosses the BOTTOM third in front of it, and red geraniums and white alyssum fill the BOTTOM LEFT corner.
shots.end: The jointed brass leg fills the CENTRE from the BOTTOM edge to the TOP edge, its riveted knee joint at the middle against the pale hazy sky.
source: to see the sight-seers about the Martian machine that stands there still
shots.turn: terror -> a curiosity behind a railing; the killer is now a sight
shots.why: The weapon that emptied London is a park exhibit; he sees both times at once.

shots.frame: Close of the narrator (grey eyes, ash-grey moustache, boater with a black band) on the summit, the hazy blue city behind him, looking out over London.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; the wind lifts the brim of his boater; his head turns toward the LEFT as he speaks
shots.camera: On the summit path in front of him, standing head height, a yard and a half from his face, an 85mm lens; hazy sun comes from the upper LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the CENTRE, his head half the frame's height, his grey eyes looking past the camera to the LEFT. The blue haze of London's roofs fills the band behind his shoulders, and the pale sky fills the TOP edge above his boater.
shots.end: The narrator's face fills the CENTRE from chin to boater brim, his head turned toward the LEFT, blue haze along the BOTTOM edge behind his collar.
source: to recall the time when I saw it all bright and clear-cut, hard and silent, under the dawn of that last great day
shots.turn: the present park -> the silent dawn of the last day; both sights overlay
shots.why: He remembers the same hill bright and silent on the last great day; the living scene and the dead one sit together in him.

shots.frame: Wide of the lamplit study seen from the windows: the wife (wide hazel eyes, thick chestnut-auburn hair, sage-green wool skirt) standing in the ajar landing door, the narrator (grey eyes, ash-grey moustache) turning in the desk chair in the left foreground.
shots.motion: The camera pans from the chart to the lamp, travelling two strides, across the whole shot; the wife steps through the door onto the Turkey carpet; the narrator turns in the desk chair toward her, his hand rising from the table
shots.camera: Beside the French windows, standing eye height, four yards from the landing door, a 28mm lens; the lamplight comes from the near LEFT and the grate glows at the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the black cast-iron fireplace at the RIGHT edge, its clock on the slate mantel under the star chart. The narrator sits in the desk chair in the BOTTOM LEFT corner beside the green-shaded lamp, his head a sixth of the frame's height, and the wife stands in the ajar landing door at the LEFT edge.
shots.end: The wife stands on the Turkey carpet at the CENTRE inside the door, the narrator turned toward her from the chair in the BOTTOM LEFT corner, the bookcases behind her.
source: And strangest of all is it to hold my wife
shots.turn: a man alone with his ghosts -> a man with company; the living one arrives
shots.why: The strangest thing of all comes in through his own door: the wife he had mourned.

shots.frame: Medium of the wife (wide hazel eyes, thick chestnut-auburn hair, sage-green wool skirt) crossing the Turkey carpet toward the desk chair, the narrator (grey eyes, ash-grey moustache) by the chair rising to meet her.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the wife as she walks across the carpet toward the narrator across the whole shot; the narrator steps out from the chair and holds out his hand; the wife reaches her hand toward his as she walks
shots.camera: Beside the bookcases at the wife's left, standing head height, two yards from her, a 40mm lens; the lamplight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the wife at the RIGHT third, her head a quarter of the frame's height, mid-stride on the carpet. The narrator stands by the desk chair at the LEFT third beside the green-shaded lamp, a yard nearer the camera and larger in the frame, and the dark window panes fill the TOP LEFT corner.
shots.end: The narrator and the wife stand a pace apart at the CENTRE by the lamp, his hand from the LEFT and hers from the RIGHT meeting between them.
source: hand again, and to think that I have counted her
shots.turn: distance -> touch; the two who counted each other dead close the gap
shots.why: She crosses to him; the reunion is a choice they keep making.

shots.frame: Medium close of the narrator (grey eyes, ash-grey moustache) and the wife (wide hazel eyes, thick chestnut-auburn hair) at the lamplit writing-table, his hand holding hers on the green leather top.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame across the whole shot; the narrator closes his fingers round the wife's hand; the wife lays her other hand over his and her thumb strokes along his knuckles
shots.camera: Across the writing-table on the window side, seated head height, a yard and a half from them, a 50mm lens; the lamplight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the two joined hands on the green leather tabletop at the BOTTOM CENTRE beside the lamp. The narrator's face sits at the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height; the wife's face sits at the RIGHT third, a little further back and smaller, her head a quarter of the frame's height.
shots.end: The narrator at the LEFT third and the wife at the RIGHT third look at each other over three clasped hands at the BOTTOM CENTRE in the green lamplight.
source: and that she has counted me, among the dead
shots.turn: counted among the dead -> held, warm and real; the living world is real here
shots.why: The answer: the one thing he can trust is her hand in his.

shots.frame: Close of the wife (wide hazel eyes, thick chestnut-auburn hair, cotton blouse with high collar) in the lamplight, her eyes lifted toward the left of the camera.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; a smile spreads at the corners of her mouth; lamplight wavers over her cheek as she speaks
shots.camera: Across the writing-table, seated head height, a yard from her face, an 85mm lens; the lamplight comes from the LEFT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the wife's face at the CENTRE, her head half the frame's height, her wide hazel eyes lifted toward the LEFT edge. The green lamp glow lights her left cheek, and the dark oak bookcases fill the TOP RIGHT corner behind her swept-up hair.
shots.end: The wife's face fills the CENTRE from brow to chin, smiling, the green lamp glow on the LEFT cheek, dark bookcases at the TOP RIGHT edge.
source: she has counted me, among the dead
shots.turn: his doubt -> her answer; the world speaks back that he is alive
shots.why: The last word belongs to the one he had mourned: she counted him dead too, and he is here.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I am ending my story, and so many of its questions are still unsettled.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Yet I write on. Carver's germs most likely killed them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Only earthly bacteria were found in their bodies, yet it stays unproven.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The Black Smoke is still unknown, and the generator of the Heat-Ray remains a puzzle.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A graver question hangs over us.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Each time Mars swings near, I expect them to try again.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: In any case, we should be prepared, and watch that planet.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Lessing believes they have already made a landing on Venus.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Our planet is no fenced, safe home for Man.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Now each shooting star that falls brings us fear.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: If they can reach Venus, so might we one day.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Or perhaps their defeat is only a reprieve.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I sit here by lamplight, and suddenly the valley below is burning again.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The house behind me stands empty.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: On the Byfleet Road, carts and children pass me, then fade like smoke.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Nights bring back the black powder.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The dead rise at me out of it, and I wake, chilled and wretched, in the dark.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I go to London.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The crowds fill Fleet Street, yet to me they are ghosts in a dead city.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Yesterday I stood on Primrose Hill among the flower beds, and I turned and reached for her hand.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Sight-seers stroll round the machine that stands there still, and children shout at their games beneath its legs.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I saw this hill bright and hard and silent, under the dawn of that last day.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: And strangest of all is the one who walks in through my study door tonight.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I hold my wife's hand again.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Each of us had counted the other among the dead.

lines.speaker: narrators_wife
lines.text: I had counted you among the dead too, my dear, and here you are, warm.
